title: Мартышка и очки
author: Иван Крылов
summary: A monkey gets hold of spectacles, cannot work out what they are for, and smashes them. Complete fable in verse.

source.editionId: Krylov, Басни, Книга первая, XVII; Wikisource revision 4797186

rights.original: Krylov (died 1844); underlying Russian work first published in 1815 and public domain.
rights.transcription: Russian transcription from Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA; source page links to its revision history and terms.
rights.translation: New English translation for Slovarchik, CC BY-SA 4.0; no published translation reused.

translationReview.method: Checked all 22 verse lines against the pinned source, divided at complete verse units, and kept the rule the source prints between the fable and its moral as the break between the two paragraphs. «Мартышка» is rendered as a monkey rather than a marmoset: Krylov means an ape of no particular species, and the English name of the animal matters less than the fact that she is vain and impatient.

sentences.ru:
Мартышка к старости слаба глазами стала;
А у людей она слыхала,
Что это зло еще не так большой руки:
Лишь стоит завести Очки.
sentences.en:
With age the Monkey’s eyes grew weak;
but she had heard from people
that this was not so great an evil after all:
you need only get hold of Spectacles.

sentences.ru:
Мартышка тут с досады и с печали
О камень так хватила их,
Что только брызги засверкали.
sentences.en:
At that the Monkey, in vexation and in grief,
dashed them against a stone so hard
that nothing flashed but the splinters.

sentences.ru:
К несчастью, то ж бывает у людей:
Как ни полезна вещь, — цены не зная ей,
Невежда про неё свой толк все к худу клонит;
А ежели невежда познатней,
Так он её ещё и гонит.
sentences.en:
Unhappily, the same thing happens among people:
however useful a thing may be, if they do not know its worth,
the ignorant will always turn their talk of it to the bad;
and if the ignorant man is of higher rank,
he will drive the thing out as well.
